user.title: Create an Entity Controller
user.description: Turns the controlled entities on when a sensor triggers, and off again once the delay has passed. More options are available after creating it.

data_description.sensors: Entities that trigger the controller, such as motion sensors.
data_description.entities: Entities turned on and off by the controller, such as lights.
data_description.delay: How long the controlled entities stay on after the sensors stop triggering.

error.invalid_name: The name must contain letters or numbers.

abort.already_configured: An Entity Controller with this name already exists.

init.title: Entity Controller options
init.description: Empty fields use their defaults. Saving applies the changes right away, without restarting Home Assistant.

data_description.sensors: Entities that trigger the controller, such as motion sensors.
data_description.entities: Entities turned on and off by the controller, such as lights.
data_description.trigger_on_activate: Turned on when the controller activates, but not turned off again, such as scripts or scenes.
data_description.trigger_on_deactivate: Turned on when the controller deactivates.
data_description.state_entities: Entities whose state the controller watches instead of the controlled entities. Leave empty to use the controlled entities.
data_description.overrides: While any of these is on, the controller does nothing.

data_description.delay: How long the controlled entities stay on after the sensors stop triggering.
data_description.sensor_type: Event sensors start the delay when they trigger. Duration sensors also keep the entities on for as long as they stay on.
data_description.sensor_resets_timer: With a duration sensor, start the delay again when the sensor turns off.
data_description.stay_mode: Once activated, keep the entities on until they are turned off by something else.
data_description.start_time: The controller only reacts between these two times. HH:MM:SS, or sunrise/sunset with an optional offset, such as `sunset - 00:30:00`.
data_description.end_time: HH:MM:SS, or sunrise/sunset with an optional offset, such as `sunset - 00:30:00`.

night_mode.name: Night mode
night_mode.description: Different delay and service data between two times. Set both times to enable it.

data_description.start_time: HH:MM:SS, or sunrise/sunset with an optional offset, such as `sunset - 00:30:00`.
data_description.end_time: HH:MM:SS, or sunrise/sunset with an optional offset, such as `sunset - 00:30:00`.
data_description.delay: Leave empty to use the main delay.
data_description.service_data: Leave empty to use the main turn on data.
data_description.service_data_off: Leave empty to use the main turn off data.

data_description.block_timeout: The controller blocks when the entities are already on, or turned on by something else, while it is active. It then leaves them alone. After this time it takes over again. Leave empty to stay blocked until they are turned off.
data_description.disable_block: Never block. Turning the entities on by hand while active restarts the delay instead.
data_description.backoff: Each new trigger while active multiplies the delay by the backoff factor.

behaviours.name: Transition behaviours
behaviours.description: What happens to the controlled entities when the controller enters or leaves a state.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Leave the state lists empty to use the defaults: on is `on`, `playing`, `home`, `True`; off is `off`, `idle`, `paused`, `away`, `False`.

data_description.state_attributes_ignore: Changes to only these attributes of the state entities are ignored.
data_description.ignored_event_sources: Regular expressions matched against the context ID of a state change. Matching changes are ignored.
